$comment: Single source of truth for the Scroll Area API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: scroll-area
title: Scroll Area
description: A box that scrolls its content, with thin scrollbars in the colours of the style. It is the browser's own scrolling, so touch, wheel, keyboard and find-in-page all work.

label.description: A name for the region, read by screen readers. Needed when nothing inside can take focus, so the box itself is in the Tab order.

children.description: The content. Give the box a height (or a width) so it has something to scroll.

examples.title: Vertical
examples.description: A fixed-height list that scrolls up and down. Click it or Tab to it, then use the arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End.

examples.title: Horizontal
examples.description: A row wider than its box, like a shelf of cards. Shift + wheel, a trackpad swipe or the arrow keys scroll it sideways.

a11y: It is native scrolling: nothing is faked, so the wheel, touch, the keyboard and assistive technology work as on any page.
The box has tabindex="0", so keyboard users can focus it and scroll with the arrow keys, Page Up/Down and Home/End. A focus ring shows when it has focus.
Because it can take focus, it has a name: role="region" with an aria-label (React: label) that says what is inside.
Scrollbars are thin, but they stay visible and draggable, in the style's colours.
